verses.1: In the fifteenth year of his reign, Rehuel became king. Yotam, son of David, became king over Judah.
verses.2: He ruled for forty years. He also ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. But he did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD, his God, just as his father David did.
verses.3: And he went along the path of the kings of Israel. And also, his son was taken away by fire, just as the nations were destroyed. This happened because Jehovah destroyed them from before the sons of Israel.
verses.4: And he burned and set them on fire in the ashes, and under every bush.
verses.5: Then Rezin, king of Israel, would rise up and take control of Jerusalem. He would lead the army against Judah, but they were unable to defeat them.
verses.6: On that day, Rezin, king of Aram, brought Eilat back to Aram. He freed the Jews from their homes and villages. Eilat settled there until today.
verses.7: And Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria, saying, “I am your servant. Please save me from the hands of the kings of Aram and of Israel who are preparing to attack me.”
verses.8: And Ahaz took the money and gold that were found in the house of Jehovah and in the treasures of the king’s palace. He sent it to the king of Assyria.
verses.9: And the king of Assyria heard of this. So he went up to Damasco. There, he captured her and revealed her secrets. And Kira and Retzin were killed.
verses.10: And King Ahaz went to Jerusalem to see the altar that was built there. He saw the altar in Damashq. Then King Ahaz sent the priest Uriah to bring back the image of the altar, along with its design for all its construction.
verses.11: And Uria, the priest, made the altar, just as the king had ordered. He did this until the king arrived.
verses.12: And the king came from Damascus. The king saw the altar, and he stepped forward toward it and stood on it.
verses.13: And he burned his offerings and his sacrifices. Then he poured out the blood of the sacrifices on the altar.
verses.14: And the idol that was set up in front of Jehovah. He brought it from among the idols and from within the house of Jehovah. Then he placed it on the path leading to the altar.
verses.15: And the king ordered Ahaz to command that the priest should burn the offerings on the altar in the morning, as well as the offerings for the king and his people. All sacrifices and offerings should be burned on that altar. And from the sacrifice of the grain offering, I will take some blood.
verses.16: And Uria, the priest, did all that which the king Ahaz commanded him to do.
verses.17: And the king took away the shutters from those doors. He removed the curtains and the water from above the sunken area below them. Then he placed it on a stone surface.
verses.18: And the Sabbath days, which we observe in the house, and the entrance of the king who is magnificent. This was a sign from Jehovah against the king of Assyria.
verses.19: And the additional words of Ahaz, which he made, are not written in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.20: And he lay down with his fathers. He was buried with his fathers in the city of David. His son Jehoshaphat became his king.
